summary: The 2786-line cross-milestone src/runtime.ts is split into explicit private subsystems without changing any public API (Issue #84): src/runtime/model.ts (config schema/types/eval+error contracts/wire limits/helpers), kernel.ts (one Python process + JSONL protocol + cell routing), bridge.ts (query/spawn/followup + cell token guard + shared input factory + continuable tracking), jobs.ts (M12 producer + per-Session slot registry), session.ts (FIFO queue, kernel map, sandbox launch, idle retention, M5/M10 checkpoint registry), plugin.ts (tool/system-prompt/teardown), and src/runtime.ts is now a thin public aggregation boundary (16 lines). The text-slice test in rlm-snapshot-io was adapted to follow the owning files, and KERNEL_PATH gained one '..' for the new directory depth. Public exports (ConfigSchema, RlmError, TOOL_NAME, createRlmRuntime, registerRlmPlugin, createRlmJobSpec, startRlmJob, types) are byte-identical in name and shape.

pointers: Issue#67 text assertions follow owning files

steps: Mapped every top-level declaration by content anchor and cut the file into six subsystems with a scripted range split, then fixed cross-module visibility (all private internals exported at module boundary) and the KERNEL_PATH depth (src/runtime/ is one directory deeper than src/).

Foreground rlm_eval and M12 jobs now consume buildRlmCodeEvalInput from one bridge module; snapshot transport/durable publication are owned by session.ts alongside the kernel map; the tool and job specs share one execution path.
Behavior unchanged: full gate PASS after the split.

evidence.target: pnpm test (full suite on split tree)

limitations: The split is mechanical and behavioral-identical; no module-level unit tests were added (public behavior is covered by the existing 270-test suite).
